Jon Gullotti contacted Phish.net in an effort to get this show circulating and it now does so thanks to him and the work of Jeff Goldberg of The Audio Specialist. Jon acquired this recording on cassette from the Penny Post's owner the week after the show. Part of the second set is missing (the music between YEM's cut jam segment and the cut into Walk Away) because Jon copied over it with live versions of the Grateful Dead's Dark Star and Shakedown (this music was on the beginning of side A of the second tape). According to Phish.com, fan reports noted that Fluffhead was performed at this show, and so it's likely that Fluffhead was one of the songs copied over; it is not clear if more than the remainder of YEM's jam segment, Fluffhead, and part of Walk Away were copied over.

Because the raw recording is so flawed (e.g., Caravan is only a fragment, YEM's jam cuts out, most of Walk Away is missing, and there are cuts at either the beginning or end of numerous songs including Weekapaug, Slave and Loew), I asked Jeff Goldberg to employ his expertise to try to create a more listenable, "remastered" version (Jeff also needed to splice the Coil and AC/DC Bag, pieces of which were on both side A and side B). Jeff's work included adjusting the pitch so that A = 440 Hz; fixing the hiccup and duplicated bar at the beginning of Mikes Song; evening-out amplitude levels that were never set during the original recording; normalizing amplitude levels to maximize bandwidth and minimize noise floor; equalizing the sound/timbre of each individual track (different parts of the tapes required different EQ curves); eliminating extreme tape hiss from offending tracks; and setting metadata for each track.

If you have any analog to digital questions (or work), feel free to contact Jeff at audiospecialists@icloud.com or on twitter @theaudiopro or google plus at the.audio.ace@gmail.com or facebook.com/theaudiospecialist.

Great thanks to Jon and Jeff for helping get this show into circulation for the first time after more than 26 years. This gives me a little hope that maybe one day my first show will circulate, too. (10/6/89) -charlie@phish.net

The cut in Harpua is unfortunate. It was at the end of the first 
set cassette and I'm not sure why it wasn't there. It went right 
from the Weekapaug to what you have here. 

The filler represents the missing portion of 4/8/90 to pair with 
Jeff Goldberg's excellent 141666 seed, albeit with a tape flip. 
The flip occurs prior to the Goldberg conclusion, so a nice crossfade 
can be done and the flip forgotten. The 1st generation copy used to 
supply this "should" sound similar, but it doesn't. Here's why. 

Eric recorded all of the Spring Colorado 1990 run, and May 23,24,and 30 1990 
in the Southeast. He used an Aiwa double well auto-reverse consumer deck. 
Eric liked to run low levels, religiously. With the low levels, the 
signal to noise level is poor.....you needed a certain amount of gain with
the 1990 board to get everything. Eric seemed to figure this out, a bit, as 
things went along. His Southeast tapes sound a little better. 

The tape heads were not particularly clean and probably were not 
demagnetized. Occurring in tandem with auto-reverse record mode
usually makes for poor results with one side sounding muddier than the other. 
There was also a fairly significant level discrepancy between channels on 
these tapes as well - I'm not exactly sure what that was about. These and 
other issues were corrected in the 24bit realm.   

Nevertheless, Eric was a cool taper. He did things that other tapers didn't 
do....he recorded long intros and outros, including capturing the house P.A. 
music pre and post-show. He recorded soundchecks. Eric's favorite songs 
were Lizards and No Dogs Allowed, which the band played for him at 4/21/90.

Where possible, I applied some slight phase cancellation over the noise to try and lessen it as much as possible without destroying the *wanted* material. I figured this master was bright enough that a lil original hiss wouldn't hurt. Using the BBE unit on this with such settings may seem a little "much", but when used in this method it acts as a Phase Correcting Limiter you could say....it really enhances the lower levels yet keeping the overall volume in check by keeping the output real low. "Anyway, as we arrived for soundcheck, there were about 10 of us hanging out under overcast skies.

Trey announced that due to the storm, they would be unable to finish the show." 

"While all were bummed (and most tripping), we understand and went back to our rooms to plan alternate activities. 
After about 30 minutes, word of mouth spread that they had agreed to play a second set in the Co-op lounge. 
All their equipment was packed away so they agree to use the gear of our campus cover band "Pi". 
When I arrived at the co-op there were about 10 of us and the set had just started.

Pizza was ordered and a keg bought and brought in and the show continued to conclusion. It was amazing."

tags.notes: This show was Phish's first public gig in New Jersey and featured many references to the state. Trey started the show by saying he was born and raised in New Jersey. Prior to Buried Alive, Trey asked for a show of hands from the sparse crowd as to how many people in the room were actually from New Jersey and said "we're going to play a song that we wrote that we think captures the spirit of New Jersey," calling it "New Jersey And You, Perfect Together," which is the state's tourism slogan (a joke he later referenced in Golgi and Contact). Trey encouraged the crowd to "sing along when the chorus comes, just like it's a big commercial, because we'll be filming this for the next New Jersey commercial."

1.notes: Trey said that this was sort of a dream come true for him and Page, who grew up in New Jersey, adding it was the first time they'd ever played in the state. Trey said "we'll do a little song here that brings us back to our New Jersey roots here... it's an old Bill Monroe song."

2.notes: Buried Alive

Stash was played by request for "Big Phil" Muller, and was preceded by Fish playing the Charlie Chan signal. Fish said "he wrote it," Trey said "probably because I wrote it," and Mike added "I think it sucks. Essentially." Regarding Stash, Trey said "I collaborated on this song writing the music end of it and the lyrics were written by another native New Jerseyian, Tom Marshall, who isn't here tonight, unfortunately, because he's gotta be at work tomorrow programming computers." Fish added "for his dad" and Trey responded "My dad, he works for my dad. Keeping it all in the family here."

3.notes: Trey said they were going to play it in honor of their first gig in New Jersey.
